[1/4] Planning: simulation-depth pass on combat and void traversal - progression-scaled encounter threat with early-boss gating, consistent evasive-burn disengagement (fuel cost, streak/combo reset), and Hollow resonance risk-reward with partial emergency payout plus CLI/REST/cockpit telemetry

impact_assessment.why: Combat difficulty never scales with player progression, a 30% anarchy dreadnought roll can ambush a level-1 hull, free evasive burns dodge the loss-aversion streak reset, and void traversal only punishes storms with no variable reward or bail-out value
impact_assessment.benefits: Keeps the combat flow channel as mastery grows, removes an early-game unfair spike, closes the streak-preserving escape exploit, and turns passive void waiting into a risk/reward loop with transparent resonance payouts
impact_assessment.risks: contract: generated enemy stats/bounties and VoidTraversalState serialization change, evasive burn gains a fuel cost; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: engine RLock retained, all new mutation stays inside it; state: resonance is an additive default-0.0 field and old saves load unchanged
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for scaling, boss gating, evasive-burn costs, resonance accrual/payouts and serialization; generate_system_enemy keeps threat_level=1 defaults so existing callers/tests are unchanged; partial emergency payout is capped below full arrival value; CLI/REST/cockpit parity and G-012 determinism verified

[1/4] Planning: exploration/resource depth pass - prevent zero-power wasted scans, reward full-system survey completion with codex progress, make derelict titanium salvage advance the advertised mining contract, and give fuel-scoop bodies a finite deterministic volatile reserve that recharges over ticks

impact_assessment.why: Exploration currently has three retention/balance gaps: a scan at 0 sensor power permanently consumes a body for no bounty, scanning every body in a system has no completion payoff, the mining contract promises salvage progress it never receives, and scooping gives unlimited free fuel at any star/gas/ice body, bypassing station fuel and trade
impact_assessment.benefits: Adds a clear Zeigarnik completion goal per system, closes a wasted-scan trap, makes contract wording truthful and salvage economically useful, and turns fuel into a local resource-management loop without removing exploration viability
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CelestialBody gains serialized volatile_tapped, scan completion adds stats/snapshot fields, and scoop availability semantics change when a reservoir is tapped out; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: engine RLock retained, system/body replacement stays inside it; state: volatile_tapped defaults to 0 and legacy saves load unchanged
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for scan gating, survey completion, salvage contract progress, reserve depletion/recharge and legacy defaults; reserve sizes derive deterministically from body type/id; existing first-scoop tests keep passing; codex metric and CLI/REST/cockpit telemetry covered; README/ADR updated

[1/2] Plan: polish the exploration pass - add a per-body volatile recharge schedule so a tap returns exactly after 6 ticks rather than on absolute tick boundaries, clamp corrupt negative volatile counters on load, expose next-tap telemetry, and cover both with regressions

impact_assessment.why: Verification found two residual correctness gaps: recharge was globally boundary-aligned (a tap could return 1-6 ticks after use), and malformed saves could keep negative volatile counters because from_dict performed no clamp
impact_assessment.benefits: Makes the fuel-reservoir simulation predictable and fair, hardens save loading, and gives players a clear next-tap countdown without changing the 3-8 reservoir balance
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CelestialBody gains volatile_recharge_tick with legacy default 0 and the scoop snapshot gains next_tap_in; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: all changes remain under the engine RLock; state: new field is additive and old saves load with a full reservoir
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure recharge helper with deterministic tests for early, exact, and large jumps; clamp tests for negative legacy payloads; save/load roundtrip; existing 483 tests and 4/4 gates rerun; ADR-039 and README synced

[1/2] Plan: harden the volatile recharge schedule against corrupt far-future timestamps - cap any due tick beyond one interval at now+6, add a pure-helper regression, and document the guard

impact_assessment.why: The second verification pass found that negative counters are clamped but a malformed far-future volatile_recharge_tick could lock a body for an unbounded time; a legitimate due can never be more than one interval ahead
impact_assessment.benefits: Removes the last identified corrupt-save lockout path without changing normal reservoir balance or scheduling
impact_assessment.risks: contract: recharge_volatile_reserve gains a defensive cap but keeps its signature and normal outputs; dependency: none; concurrency: pure helper, no state mutation; state: no schema change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first pure-helper test for a far-future due tick, rerun all 486 tests plus the new regression, 4/4 project gates, README/ADR sync
